sections.html:
Revere is a dense coastal city in Suffolk County, about five miles northeast of downtown Boston, and the end of the MBTA Blue Line. The 2020 census counted 62,186 people on 10.13 square miles, of which 4.43 square miles are water, so much of the city is marsh, beach and harbor edge. Winthrop, Chelsea, East Boston, Everett, Malden, Saugus and Lynn are the neighbors, with Massachusetts Bay to the east.

Roughly 10,900 people live on each square mile, so lots are tight and several districts mix single-family and multi-family houses. The census found 23,050 households and 24,539 housing units, 6.1 percent of them vacant. A homeowner vacancy rate of 0.6 percent means very few owner homes sat empty and for sale.

Revere began as Rumney Marsh, was part of Boston from 1632 and then Chelsea, and split off as North Chelsea in 1846. It took the name Revere in 1871 and became a city after a 1914 vote. Railroad lines, the Eastern Railroad in 1838 and the Boston, Revere Beach and Lynn Railroad in 1875, set off rapid growth. That first boom is when most of Revere filled in, so older houses are common.

Each district has a different housing mix, so name yours when you describe the house.

  • Beachmont: the eastern edge near East Boston's Orient Heights, with single and multi-family homes and a Blue Line stop.
  • Revere Beach Boulevard: apartment complexes, restaurants and some single-family houses along the three-mile beach, with newer development adding luxury apartments.
  • Point of Pines and Oak Island: the north end of the beach, mostly single and multi-family homes beside the marsh and wetlands.
  • Shirley Avenue: the most ethnically diverse part of the city, with ethnic groceries, restaurants and community services.
  • Broadway and Revere Street: the central civic and commercial arteries that connect City Hall to the beach.
  • West Revere: single and multi-family homes plus the Squire Road business district with large shopping plazas and hotels.

A beachfront condo and a West Revere two-family attract different people, so match the pitch to the district.

The Blue Line ends in Revere, with three stations: Wonderland, Revere Beach and Beachmont. Houses within walking distance of a station can be easier to market to commuters who work in Boston. U.S. Route 1 and state routes 1A, 16, 60, 107 and 145 run through the city.

When you list or sell, give the station name and the walking time. Buyers searching for a Blue Line home compare those details first. A new Revere High School is under construction at the former Wonderland Greyhound Park site, where ground was broken in August 2025, so the area around Wonderland is changing.

Revere sits only about 20 feet above sea level, with marsh and ocean on several sides. Two events show why buyers watch storms: the Blizzard of 1978 destroyed many of the beach's remaining businesses, and an EF2 tornado came through Chelsea and into Revere on July 28, 2014, damaging many buildings, City Hall among them.

The year-round temperature range is roughly 23 to 82 degrees Fahrenheit, with snow lasting about five months and the muggiest stretch running from mid-June to late September. If your house is near the beach or the marsh, ask your insurer and the city building office about flood zone status before listing, so you know the answer before a buyer asks.

State rules set the checklist. Your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms must pass a fire department inspection, and the department issues a certificate of compliance for the sale or transfer. Alarms more than ten years old, or with no date, have to be replaced. The department charges for the inspection, so call once a closing date is set. See the Mass.gov guidance.

Massachusetts also taxes deeds by statute. The base rate in G.L. c. 64D, section 1 is $2 per $500 of price, and your attorney can confirm the amount for your sale.

Revere's Assessors Department is at 281 Broadway. You can call 781-286-8170 or write to assessors@revere.org. The city lists senior, blind and hardship exemptions on its assessors page. Each requires ownership and occupancy, and if the property is in a trust the applicant must be both trustee and beneficiary or hold a life estate.

Ask the assessors whether an exemption on your bill affects the closing, and give the latest bill to your attorney.

sections.h2: If your assessment looks too high
sections.html:
• Pay every tax installment on time. The Appellate Tax Board treats timely payment as a condition for hearing an appeal.
  • File an abatement application with the assessors by the first installment due date printed on your bill.
  • Wait up to three months for a decision, then appeal to the board within three months of that decision or of the deemed denial.
  • Bring comparable sales and photographs of similar nearby houses.

The burden is on the owner, so a short, evidence-based case does better than a general complaint. The board's guide explains each step.

A few steps in a sensible order save time on a Revere sale.

  • Pull your latest tax bill and call the assessors if an exemption is involved.
  • Check the age of every smoke and carbon monoxide alarm and replace the old ones.
  • Book the fire department inspection as soon as a closing date is set.
  • Write down anything you know about water, storm damage or flood zone status.
  • Give the deed, any mortgage payoff figure and estate paperwork to your attorney.

Houses here range from older mill-era and early twentieth century buildings to newer beachfront apartments, so condition varies a lot. Tight lots and shared walls in multi-family houses can also affect access for repairs and showings, which is one reason some owners prefer a single visit from a cash buyer to weeks of open houses.

sections.h2: Ways to sell a Revere house
sections.html:
A traditional listing, a sale on your own and a cash sale are the three routes. Which fits depends on repairs, timing and how much effort you can give.

  • A listing exposes the house to the most buyers but brings showings, inspection negotiations and a timeline set by the buyer's lender.
  • A cash sale can close on a schedule you choose, and the buyer takes the house in its present condition.

If your house needs work, a cash buyer may make more sense than spending months on repairs, and you can compare both routes before deciding. Cash Home Buyers can look at a Revere house as it stands, and the offer carries no obligation. Ask for a closing date that fits your plans, and keep the fire certificate and recording steps on your list whichever route you take. If tenants live in one unit of a multi-family house, say so at the start so everyone can plan around them.

faqs.a: Revere is in Suffolk County, about five miles northeast of downtown Boston.

faqs.q: How many people live in Revere?

faqs.a: The Blue Line ends in Revere with stations at Wonderland, Revere Beach and Beachmont.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Revere?
faqs.a: Yes. The local fire department has to issue a certificate of compliance for a sale or transfer of a home.

faqs.q: Who handles property assessments in Revere?
faqs.a: The Assessors Department at 281 Broadway, reachable at 781-286-8170 or assessors@revere.org.
